newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas prices extend losses.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas prices extend losses.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices continued to soften Tuesday, as milder temperatures and ample storage supplies in the East kept many buyers away from the spot market, sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, gas traded mostly in the C$2.57-2.62 per gigajoule (GJ) range, falling about 10 cents from Monday's trading range but recovering from yesterday's lows in the C$2.40s.
The return of cold weather to Alberta was the main supporting factor in the market, traders said. Temperatures in Calgary today were reaching highs around -11 degrees Celsius.
The bitter cold is forecast to continue throughout this week, with lows of -25 degrees C expected Friday.
February AECO prices slipped to about C$2.73 per GJ, from the C$2.80-2.85 range on Monday. Summer prices were also lower at C$1.62.
"It's cold, but terms are corresponding to Henry Hub," one Calgary-based trader said.

NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas futures slipped to a low of $2.83 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), down 24 cents from Monday. As the closing neared, the contract recovered to the low-$2.90s.

At Sumas, Wash., milder temperatures in California and weaker power prices took their toll on prices. Traders reported closing most deals in the $2.34-2.39 per mmBtu range, down about five to 10 cents.
At Niagara, prices tumbled another 30 cents to about $3.10 per mmBtu as warmer air moved into the region and many buyers withdrew gas from storage to meet demand.
